evidence.quote: Let's keep this one tight — I want to come out of it with the cutover shape actually decided, because the steering group asks again on Thursday

observations.why: Tanya sets a firm agenda constraint by invoking executive steering committee pressure and deadlines.

evidence.quote: Hold those for ten minutes. Sequencing first. Tina, you've been living in the site plan — where are we?

observations.why: Tanya exercises meeting control (procedural authority) and invites Tina to lead the situational assessment.

evidence.quote: Then let me say where I've landed, because I don't think I'm going to move off it. We do this one site at a time.

observations.why: Tanya establishes a firm organizational decision through her role authority.

evidence.quote: Can I push on it for a second? Not because I disagree — because the steering group will push and I'd rather they push here.

observations.why: Xavier explicitly seeks permission to stress-test the decision through red-teaming.

evidence.quote: Running two systems at one desk for a few weeks is a known, contained pain with a named owner. Two cutovers landing in the same week is an unbounded one, and we've got nobody to hand it to.

observations.why: Tanya justifies the decision using a rational trade-off between bounded and unbounded risk.

evidence.quote: The soak is two full weeks. That's the Dockside number, and I'd hold us to it.

observations.why: Tina uses empirical benchmark data from the Dockside pilot to set a technical standard.

evidence.quote: So the position I want us to take is: during cutover, every reporting read comes off the replica. Not "should", not "where possible" — reporting does not touch the live system during a cutover window, full stop.

observations.why: Xavier leverages technical expertise and outage analysis to argue for a strict operational rule.

evidence.quote: Then that's the rule. Reporting reads come off the replica during cutover. Xavier, write it into the runbook as a rule and not as guidance

observations.why: Tanya codifies the recommendation into an official rule and assigns action items via positional authority.

evidence.quote: The vendor stays the system of record for reference data until the last site is live. Every site reads from the vendor's copy, we mirror it read-only, and we take ownership on the day Clyde goes green and not a day earlier.

observations.why: Xavier articulates a technical policy based on data governance expertise.

evidence.quote: Because if we take ownership at site one, we've got two sites on our reference data and two on theirs, and the zone map drifts between them.

observations.why: Xavier provides cause-and-effect logical reasoning to defend his architectural stance.
